sentences.text: Paluxysuchus was an extinct neosuchian crocodyliform with a long, flat, and triangular skull that likely represents a transitional form between early and later neosuchian shapes. Unlike most primitive longirostrine neosuchians which had tubular snouts, this animal possessed a flattened snout considered a primitive trait among its group.

The most complete skull fossil measures about 30 cm in length and features enlarged teeth at the tip of its snout. It also possessed a postorbital process with an elongated prong bordering the side of the eye socket.
The most complete skull fossil of Paluxysuchus measures about 30 cm in length.
Paluxysuchus had enlarged teeth at the tip of its snout.

The genus Paluxysuchus contains only one species, Paluxysuchus newmani, which was named after Kent Newman, who helped excavate and prepare fossils from the Hood County ranch. Paluxysuchus was the second crocodyliform named from the Early Cretaceous of Texas, following Pachycheilosuchus.

Paluxysuchus belongs to the clade Neosuchia, which includes modern crocodilians and their extinct relatives dating back to the Early Jurassic. It is a basal member of Neosuchia, representing one of the earliest branches in the group, though not the oldest. Phylogenetic analysis places Paluxysuchus just outside the group of "derived" neosuchians, which includes modern crocodilians and forms with shortened snouts. The animal belongs to the family Paluxysuchidae.
Paluxysuchus lived during the Aptian to Albian stages, approximately 119.57 to 100.5 million years ago.
